correctness.rationale: The proof constructs the 16-vertex, 40-edge stable-curve dual graph from divisor intersection classes, identifies the rank-25 torus character lattice with its integral cycle lattice, and derives signed Frobenius matrices for all seven S5 cycle representatives. All seven matrices are unimodular finite-order actions. The included exact Z[u] elementary row-column algorithm reduces uI-G to the claimed diagonal factors by operations invertible at every integer u, and five independent integer Smith-form specializations per case match. The resultant finite abelian groups hold for every prime power q whenever the point configuration exists. Finite numerical checks are supportive, not a substitute for the symbolic proof.

originality.rationale: The exact statement concerns the complete group of F_q-rational points of the connected Picard torus of the sixteen-curve quartic del Pezzo boundary in each of six non-five-cycle permutation types. The five-cycle case is prior work, not newly claimed. Accessible source comparisons and semantic searches did not reveal the other six invariant-factor decompositions, even though the graph geometry, torus character lattice theory, and several group orders are prior-implied. Residual unindexed historical overlap remains possible.

value.rationale: The 16-curve boundary is a geometrically intrinsic stable divisor on a quartic del Pezzo surface. The six complete rational-point groups, uniform in q and seven geometric Frobenius cycle patterns with one known case identified, refine the known zeta/order and five-cycle torus result. The nontrivial mixed-cycle 2-primary gluing in odd characteristic is genuine integral arithmetic information not encoded in rational Frobenius eigenvalues. Exact finite-group structure can support future descent and generalized-Jacobian studies without presuming a downstream theorem.
